{'index': 0, 'translation': 'Apple is reportedly piloting a brand-new "Live Notes" system in select retail stores. According to the latest reports, the system uses artificial intelligence (AI) to record and transcribe conversations between Genius Bar staff and customers.\n'}

{'index': 1, 'translation': 'In the latest edition of his *Power On* newsletter, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reported that the Live Notes system lets Apple Store employees "record conversations via an AI tool, and transcribe and summarise discussions with customers."\n'}

{'index': 2, 'translation': "These transcriptions are then stored in Apple's internal Genius Bar system. According to Bloomberg, the aim is to let staff focus on serving customers without having to split their attention on taking notes.\n"}

{'index': 3, 'translation': "It's said that before a Genius Bar session begins recording, both the employee and the customer must agree and opt in.\n"}

{'index': 4, 'translation': 'However, Apple retail employees have reportedly raised concerns about how the Live Notes system might be used going forward:\n'}

{'index': 5, 'translation': 'As of now, Live Notes is not mandatory. According to Bloomberg, Apple is "unable to determine at this point" whether it will roll the system out to more stores, make it compulsory, or change how the transcriptions are used.\n'}
